svg.title: Shadewright analyzer
svg.desc: Zoom into the analyzer identity. Built: the collector watches events, pod status and, for the symptom sources of active modules, HPAs, pods and the KEDA, Flux and Kyverno kinds the chart grants (a KEDA replica ceiling becomes an Incident about the ScaledObject, a cloudflared replica not ready for 2 minutes one about its Deployment) in the watched namespaces, resolves owners (dropping the evidence of pods whose workload has retired their template and the readiness or startup probe failures that are part of a pod's start or shutdown), holds a BackOff or Unhealthy event whose pod status shows no cause for 2 minutes and drops it if the container recovered, and one whose pod status shows a cause until the Incident controller tells the collector it has seen that cause (no poll), at most 2 minutes, then emits it with its cause, redacts and fingerprints them; two levels of deduplication feed a durable, bounded Incident CR; the analysis trigger decides when an Incident is due. The trigger reads spec.analysis.maxAnalysesPerDay from the RemediationSettings and reads and updates the daily count in the Budget ConfigMap shadewright-analysis-budget in the operator namespace; an unreadable budget means not due. Separately, the analyzer reports platform and integration detection in the settings status; no component reads that status to decide anything. Prometheus (approved templates, watched namespaces, optional with --prometheus-url) and pod logs (bounded, redacted, watched namespaces, get on pods/log through the watch role) have adapters that the analyzer creates and gives to the context builder. The context builder takes selected data from the sources and makes a bounded (48 KiB), redacted context in provenance-tagged blocks. The analysis loop runs only when the analyzer is started with --triage-model (off by default): when an Incident is due it claims it (phase Analyzing, identified by lastAnalysisTime), builds the context, takes one unit of the daily budget, makes one structured call to the triage model and, on a deterministic escalation signal only, calls the escalation model with the read tools bound to the incident's namespace; it refuses a reply from another model than the configured one, validates the result against the schema, takes the previous memory limit from the pod template and the previous maxReplicaCount from the ScaledObject it read once before the call (a ScaledObject that is not ready is not offered that action and ends ScalerNotReady), checks the catalog, rechecks its claim live and creates the typed RemediationRequest for the executor, or hands off to a person. The model provider outside the cluster is reached through the configured provider, only at an endpoint inside the operator's host allow-list, with the analyzer's workload identity. Caps on the Incident: 256 held per Incident, 2,500 per source namespace, at most 500 Incidents. The analysis trigger also applies a debounce and a cooldown. With no evidence the analyzer proposes nothing and hands off to a human. The model provider gets a redacted, bounded context and returns one structured result; it has no tools with write access, and it is reached through the host allow-list and the workload identity. The Prometheus and pod log adapters are wired to the context builder only. Caps on the Incident: 256 held per Incident, 2,500 per source namespace, at most 500 Incidents. svg.text: Teal: outside the analyzer. The analyzer identity is read-only plus the model.
